clue.text: Meal — I get it cooked, OK?

indicators.note: food that is cooked is worked over, and figuratively cooked figures are fiddled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks they have understood a recipe for a meal before agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters of MEAL, I, GET and IT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lawful or acceptable is fine, all right, above board.

clue.text: Want some special acknowledgement

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone craves a little particular recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: want as a noun or verb means absence or shortage of something.

clue.text: Soldier to be in Caribbean location shortly? That is right

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the island is dropped

parts.note: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to be posted to a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of a guards regiment, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: Sailor with old books that may have mystical signs

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sailor carries ancient texts covered in arcane symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-telling cards bear occult symbols such as the Hanged Man and the Tower.

clue.text: Doctor, wise man accommodating fool

indicators.note: says the wise man has room inside for the fool

parts.note: a mage is a magus, a learned wise man
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A physician and a sage put up an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb, to falsify figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To massage figures is to manipulate or falsify them, just as one doctors accounts.

clue.text: Performance cancelled — something discouraging

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance
an event that is off has been called off

explanation.surface: A cancelled show is a real disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a thing that puts someone off or repels their interest.

clue.text: Stone or piece of broken glass possibly hard to remove

indicators.note: says the letter for hard is taken out of the fragment word

parts.note: a shard is a sharp fragment, glass being one example
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone is deciding whether a hard bit in something is a stone or a sliver of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sard is a reddish-brown variety of chalcedony, a semiprecious gemstone.

clue.text: Panic in the manner of fighting corps

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
RM is the Royal Marines, a fighting corps

explanation.surface: Fear spreads in the style of an army unit in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sudden fear or anxiety, as in 'cause alarm'.

clue.text: Musical instruction gets unintelligent one undone, confused

parts.note: dim means stupid
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: A dull-witted person is bewildered by being undone.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian score marking telling players to grow gradually softer.

clue.text: Fashionable top female to rave, never able to be wrong

parts.note: in means trendy, as in 'the in thing'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the top woman in Britain
to rant is to rave or talk wildly

explanation.surface: A stylish leading lady holds forth as though she were infallible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: infallible, incapable of error.

clue.text: Joy in church always

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A worshipper finds constant happiness at church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: gladness or good spirits, as in 'full of good cheer'.

clue.text: Astronaut switching components using a lot of force

indicators.note: the two parts of the surname, ARM and STRONG, trade places

parts.note: Neil Armstrong, the first man on the Moon

explanation.surface: An astronaut swaps out parts of his craft with brute effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong-arm tactics are coercive, relying on intimidation or physical pressure.

clue.text: One of the 19 against entering that foreign city

indicators.note: says the word for against goes inside the starchy food

parts.note: sago is a starchy food, one of the cereals of 19 across
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Something from a list of breakfast foods is barred from a foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile, a city abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Native seen as upright type

definitions.meaning: someone born in the Italian capital
the ordinary non-italic typeface, upright rather than sloping

explanation.surface: A local is described as a person of upstanding character.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman means a citizen of Rome, and also the standard vertical printing font as opposed to italic.

clue.text: Spot when king leaves castle — fantastic things worth looking at

indicators.note: the monarch's letter departs from the small spot word

parts.note: a speck is a tiny spot
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly changed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: In chess, one spots the moment the king castles and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable sights or shows, impressive displays that draw the eye.

clue.text: Leader of people inclined to be flexible

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: liable means apt or inclined to do something

explanation.surface: A political leader likes to bend with popular opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: easily bent or persuaded, supple and yielding.

clue.text: Suffering from a bruising defeat?

parts.note: a heavy sporting loss is described as bruising, but taken literally it means having been physically assaulted

explanation.surface: A sports team reeling after a heavy loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaulted and left injured, literally bruised by an attacker's fists.

clue.text: One beloved Scotsman maybe about to come into money

indicators.note: says the name and the about letter go inside the payment word

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service
Ian is a typically Scottish first name
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Scottish sweetheart is about to inherit a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged to be married is her partner's betrothed, someone dearly loved.

clue.text: Race to get first for keen professional?

parts.note: to career is to rush or race along
1st, read as IST, abbreviates first

explanation.surface: A competitor sprints to be in front, eager to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ambitious mainly for advancement at work.

clue.text: The Archers and such, say, on the radio? We gobble them up!

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken rather than written
broadcast speech is heard, not seen, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera, a serial broadcast in episodes

explanation.surface: Fans of a radio soap declare they devour every episode.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio drama about farming folk; the 'We' of the definition is the eaters, not the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast grains such as cornflakes are food people eat, so the eaters gobble them up.

clue.text: Artists turned up to eat fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Painters arrive to have a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish of the herring family, often tinned.

clue.text: Changed key before band's final piece

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: the final piece of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A group changes the key ahead of the last number in their set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests music to match 'band', but it is the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: modified or made different.

clue.text: American sitting in a tree, unusually ascetic

indicators.note: says the American letters sit inside the rearranged letters
unusual order means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: An American perched in a tree lives a strangely spartan life.
explanation.walkthrough: The perched American is pure scenery: 'unusually' makes ATERE and 'sitting in' drops the country's letters into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: severely self-disciplined and plain, avoiding comfort.

clue.text: Way of looking at something that could be right

definitions.meaning: a viewpoint or slant on a story
a right one is ninety degrees, so this is something that may be right

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a particular viewpoint might be correct.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a perspective on an issue, and a right one is a ninety-degree geometric figure.

clue.text: Endless sport leading to graduate getting low grade?

indicators.note: a word with no end has lost its closing letter, so the sport word is cut short

parts.note: a game is a sport
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Endless sport leads a student to a poor mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In British marking schemes, gamma is a low grade, after alpha and beta.
explanation.definitionFit: The third Greek letter, used in British universities for a poor third-class mark.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed about condition being mentioned again

indicators.note: says the blushing colour goes around the condition word

parts.note: a blushing person is red-faced
a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: Someone blushes when their medical condition is brought up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: said once more, repeated in words.

clue.text: Greek author upset water on work

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A Greek writer knocks water over his manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist credited with the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Distance spanned by mountain chain

indicators.note: the letters are bridged across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: How far a range of mountains stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A small imperial unit of length, about two and a half centimetres.

clue.text: Learner is not half timid type going around in mini? No!

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: only half of the two-letter word is kept, its front letter
says the timid creature goes around the little word given next

parts.note: a mouse is a proverbially timid person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous learner driver goes round in a small car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a famously small British car; the definition says the answer is anything but small.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretched luxury car is the opposite of a compact little vehicle, hence emphatically not a mini.

clue.text: Male about 101 — young member of family!

indicators.note: says the male child word goes around the numeral

parts.note: a son is a male child
CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man of about a hundred and one is called a youngster of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a descendant or heir, especially of a noble family.

clue.text: Second method to gain supremacy

parts.note: a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: Advice on a backup plan for winning dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: control or dominating influence, as in 'held sway'.

clue.text: Female always quiet with desire shows great excitement

parts.note: ever means always
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A woman who is forever silent with longing betrays her strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the highest pitch of agitation or enthusiasm, as of a frenzied crowd.
